records.question: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
search_queries: How long can a J-1 master's student do Academic Training?
records.answer:
A J-1 master's student can do up to **18 months** of Academic Training (AT), or the length of their degree program, whichever is shorter. Students pursuing a STEM degree may qualify for a special extension. ([ISSS Academic Training page](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/current-students/employment/j1-employment))

Key conditions from ISSS:
- AT during your studies and AT after your program ends are added together toward the total. Full-time and part-time AT count equally.
- The total employment/training period can't exceed the length of your academic program.
- AT must be approved and listed on your DS-2019 before your program end date, and it must start no later than 30 days after your program ends.
- Submit the Academic Training form to ISSS at least 30 days before your DS-2019 end date. ISSS recommends allowing about three weeks for processing. The form is on the [ISSS Student Portal](https://drexel0.sharepoint.com/sites/ISSS-StudentPortal/SitePages/ISSS-Student-Forms.aspx).

**Rule change to be aware of:** DHS published a final rule eliminating "duration of status" on July 17, 2026. It was scheduled to take effect September 15, and it would have required J-1 students to apply to USCIS for an extension for post-completion AT. On September 14, 2026, a federal court [postponed the effective date](https://drexel.edu/studentlife/student-success/international-student-support/announcements/2026/September/US-District-Court-Postpones-Effective-Date-of-DHS-Final-Rule-on-Duration-of-Status) and barred DHS from implementing the rule. ISSS is monitoring the situation.

For your own situation, including the STEM extension, please confirm with an ISSS advisor.

grade.explanation: The 18-month limit (or program length if shorter) is correct. However, the answer says the final DHS rule would have required J-1 students to apply to USCIS for post-completion AT, but the final-rule excerpt mentions only OPT; the AT requirement appears only in the 2025 proposed rule. It also says ISSS recommends about three weeks for processing, whereas the source recommends submitting three weeks in advance, with review taking 4–5 business days.
